name: Gemini VI-A and VII orbital rendezvous
description: Two independently crewed spacecraft met and remained in proximity in Earth orbit.

impact.note: A new ability within one space programme; docking, lunar-orbit rendezvous and station assembly in that programme all built on it.

places.note: Place is a modern geographic reference to the cited episode; it does not imply exclusive origin.

date.basis: Date stated by the cited source.

events.statement: The crewed Gemini VI-A and Gemini VII spacecraft rendezvoused in Earth orbit.
events.caveats: The rendezvous did not include docking; the two missions had distinct crews and tasks.

evidence.supports: The crewed Gemini VI-A and Gemini VII spacecraft rendezvoused in Earth orbit.
NASA history describes the five-hour formation flight.
NASA mission history identifies the agency and missions.

earliest_record.rationale: The first sourced event for this particular record, not a claim of a worldwide first.

caveats: This was rendezvous, not docking; a particular dependency on Apollo 11 is not assumed without mission-specific evidence.

measures.subject: Gemini VI-A and VII
measures.conditions: NASA historical summary; approximate reported formation time, not total mission duration.

research.note: Initial sourced admission; interpretation awaits independent review. Independent review checked event source passages and, where marked, measures and relationship scope; other facets retain prior status.
